The enrollment phase uses out-of-band channels for initial device pairing, exchanging a device ID, friendly name, static public key, and authentication secret. This secret can be a pre-shared key or a short authentication string to prevent man-in-the-middle attacks. Mutual authentication and session transport will rely on either a direct WireGuard layer or Noise_IK channel.

Session re-establishment is automated via mDNS, BLE beacons, or WireGuard endpoint heartbeat to trigger a 1-RTT handshake between devices, requiring no user input. Revocation can be initiated by either device.


Peer revocation involves removing the peer's public key from the authorized peers database or WireGuard configuration. A revocation tombstone packet, signed by the revoking device, will be broadcast over the authenticated channel if the peer is reachable; otherwise, the local key removal ensures cryptographic handshake failure on any future connection attempts.
